variables.name: VERSION
variables.comment:
* A non-decreasing version number. * *

The version number should increase any time the Encoder has a user-visible functional change * to any of encoding algorithms or the interpretation of the input parameters.

variables.name: MIN_USER_SECRET_BYTES
variables.comment: * Minimum length required for the user secret, in bytes.

variables.name: MAX_BITS
MAX_BLOOM_HASHES
variables.comment:
* Maximum number of Bloom filter hashes used for RAPPOR-encoded strings. * *

This is constrained in the current implementation by requiring 2 bytes from an MD5 value * (which is 16 bytes long) for each Bloom filter hash.

variables.name: MAX_COHORTS
variables.comment: * Maximum number of cohorts supported.

variables.name: HMAC_DRBG_TYPE_COHORT
variables.comment: * First (and only) byte of HMAC_DRBG personalization strings used to generate the cohort number.

variables.name: HMAC_DRBG_TYPE_PRR
variables.comment: * First byte of HMAC_DRBG personalization strings used to generate the PRR response.

variables.name: encoderIdBytes
variables.comment:
* A unique identifier for this Encoder, represented in UTF-8. * *

The (userSecret, encoderId) pair identify a the logical memoization table used for RAPPOR's * Permanent Randomized Response stage. Therefore, for any userSecret, each Encoder must have a * distinct identifier for Permanent Randomized Response to be effective. * *

In practice, "memoization" is achieved by generating deterministic pseudo-random bits using * HMAC_DRBG. encoderIdBytes is used as part of the personalization string.

variables.name: probabilityF
variables.comment:
* The RAPPOR "f" probability, on the range [0.0, 1.0]. * *

This it the probability of replacing a bit from the input with a uniform random bit when * generating the permanent randomized response. * *

Setting probabilityF to 0 disables the PRR phase of RAPPOR.

variables.name: probabilityP
variables.comment:
* The RAPPOR "p" probability, on the range [0.0, 1.0]. * *

This is the probability of emitting a '1' bit in the instantaneous randomized response, * given that the corresponding bit in the permanent randomized response is '0'. * *

Setting probabilityP to 0.0 and probabilityQ to 1.0 disables the IRR phase of RAPPOR.

variables.name: probabilityQ
variables.comment:
* The RAPPOR "1" probability, on the range [0.0, 1.0]. * *

This is the probability of emitting a 1 bit in the instantaneous randomized response, given * that the corresponding bit in the permanent randomized response is 1. * *

Setting probabilityP to 0.0 and probabilityQ to 1.0 disables the IRR phase of RAPPOR.

variables.name: numBits
variables.comment:
* The number of bits in the RAPPOR-encoded report. * *

Must satisfy 1 <= numBits <= MAX_BITS. * *

    *
  • For encodeOrdinal, requires 0 <= ordinal < numBits. *
  • For encodeString, uses a numBits-wide Bloom filter. *
  • For encodeBits, only the low-order numBits may be non-zero. *

variables.name: numBloomHashes
variables.comment:
* The number of hash functions used forming the Bloom filter encoding of a string. * *

Must satisfy 1 <= numBloomHashes <= MAX_BLOOM_HASHES.

variables.name: numCohorts
variables.comment: * The number of cohorts used for cohort assignment.

variables.name: cohort
variables.comment:
* The cohort this user is assigned to for Bloom filter string encoding. * *

This value is stable for a given (userSecret, numCohorts) pair. Furthermore, if two * encoders use the same userSecret but have different numCohorts values, the cohort assignment * for the encoder with the smaller numCohorts value is a bitwise suffix of the cohort assignment * for the encoder with the larger numCohorts value. It follows that, if you know maximum cohort * assignment across a set of encoders, and you know the numCohorts setting for each encoder, then * you can deduce the cohort assignment for each encoder by taking the bitwise-and of the max * cohort value and (numCohorts-1), noting that numCohorts is required to be a positive power of * 2.

variables.name: inputMask
variables.comment:
* A bitmask with 1 bits in all the positions where a RAPPOR-encoded report could have a 1 bit. * *

The bitmask has the lowest order numBits set to 1 and the rest 0.

methods.name: public String getEncoderId()
methods.comment: * Returns the Encoder ID as a UTF-8 formatted string.

methods.name: public byte[] encodeBoolean(boolean bool)
methods.comment:
* Encodes a boolean into a RAPPOR report. * *

The boolean is 0 or 1, then encoded using permanent and instantaneous randomized response. * *

In most cases, numBits should be 1 when using this method.

methods.name: public byte[] encodeOrdinal(int ordinal)
methods.comment:
* Encodes an ordinal into a RAPPOR report. * *

The ordinal is represented using a 1-hot binary representation, then encoded using permanent * and instantaneous randomized response. * * @param ordinal A value on the range [0, numBits).

methods.name: public byte[] encodeString(String string)
methods.comment:
* Encodes a string into a RAPPOR report. * *

The string is represented using a Bloom filter with numBloomHashes hash functions, then * encoded using permanent and instantaneous randomized response. * * @param string An arbitrary string.

methods.name: public byte[] encodeBits(byte[] bits)
methods.comment:
* Encodes an arbitrary bitstring into a RAPPOR report.
   *
   * @param bits A bitstring in which only the least significant numBits bits may be 1.

methods.name: private byte[] encodeBits(BitSet bits)
methods.comment:
* Encodes an arbitrary bitstring into a RAPPOR report.
   *
   * @param bits A bitstring in which only the least significant numBits bits may be 1.

methods.name: private BitSet computePermanentRandomizedResponse(BitSet bits)
methods.comment:
* Returns the permanent randomized response for the given bits. * *

The response for a particular bits input is guaranteed to always be the same for any encoder * constructed with the same parameters (including the encoderId and the userSecret).

methods.name: private BitSet computeInstantaneousRandomizedResponse(BitSet bits)
methods.comment:
* Returns the instantaneous randomized response for the given bits. * *

The instantaneous response is NOT memoized -- it is sampled randomly on * every invocation.
